notes: Conflict rules fire on trait pairs across the traits of every source a direction draws from (archetype traits, and for composed palettes the traits of the vocabulary words they were composed from). severity tension = workable; clash = recommend choosing one side. Neither ever blocks. 'variants' are checked in order; the first whose 'when' matches replaces 'resolution'. Supported 'when' keys: user_accent (true when the accent was set by the user, source user or described), density (list of density ids of the working direction).

rules.tradeoff: Cold reads as capable and exact; warm reads as human. Mixed evenly, it feels undecided.
rules.resolution: Pick one as the base. Let the other appear only in the accent color and the tone of the copy.

rules.tradeoff: Density shows everything at once; space makes each thing feel important. You can't have both on the same screen.
rules.resolution: Use density for data views and space for summaries and empty states. Never both in one panel.

rules.tradeoff: Playfulness signals low stakes; institutional design signals that mistakes matter. People trust one or the other.
rules.resolution: Choose based on what happens if the user makes an error. If it's serious, drop the playfulness.

rules.tradeoff: Premium relies on restraint; playfulness relies on surprise. Too much of either cancels the other.
rules.resolution: Keep the premium base. Allow one playful moment, such as a single animation or illustration, and nowhere else.

rules.tradeoff: Saturated color asks for attention; sober design earns trust by not asking.
rules.resolution: Keep the sober palette. Use the bright color only for the primary action.

rules.tradeoff: Expressive design adds character through decoration; minimal design removes everything that isn't needed.
rules.resolution: Let typography carry the expression. Keep color, borders, and shapes minimal.

variants.resolution: Let the accent color carry the expression, since it was the user's choice. Keep type, borders, and shapes minimal.

rules.tradeoff: Editorial layouts are built for reading one thing well; dense layouts are built for scanning many things.
rules.resolution: Use editorial type and measure for long text, and a compact table for data. Keep them in separate sections.

rules.tradeoff: Literary type slows the reader down; technical interfaces want them to move fast.
rules.resolution: Use the literary face for headings and prose only. Use a neutral sans for numbers, labels, and controls.

rules.tradeoff: Stark design creates distance on purpose; approachable design removes it.
rules.resolution: Decide who the audience is. If it's a general audience, drop the starkness.

rules.tradeoff: Experimental layouts make people work to understand; institutional design must never make them work.
rules.resolution: Keep the institutional structure. Express the experimental side only in imagery or a single display typeface.

rules.tradeoff: Rugged reads as built for use; premium reads as built to be admired.
rules.resolution: Keep rugged materials and functional layout, with premium spacing and type.

rules.tradeoff: Industrial design shows its mechanics; calm design hides them.
rules.resolution: Keep the industrial grid and labeling, and soften color and motion.

rules.tradeoff: Mechanical motion is precise and immediate; emotive motion has weight and feeling.
rules.resolution: Choose one motion character for the whole product. Don't mix snappy and springy.

rules.tradeoff: Graphic design leads with shapes and contrast; literary design leads with words.
rules.resolution: Pick which leads on each page: a graphic opener, then literary body, never both competing.

rules.tradeoff: Sensory design invites lingering; functional design gets you out fast.
rules.resolution: Put sensory moments on entry and summary screens. Keep task screens functional.

rules.tradeoff: Precision implies exact grids and hard edges; natural implies irregular, organic forms.
rules.resolution: Keep a precise grid and tight corners. Let the natural side come through color only.

rules.tradeoff: Calm needs room; density removes it.
rules.resolution: Keep the dense layout for lists and tables. Make it calm through quiet color, few borders, and no motion beyond state changes.

variants.resolution: Keep the roomy layout. Put the items people check most at the top so nothing important needs scrolling.

rules.tradeoff: Bright color warms a cold system and can make it look like two products.
rules.resolution: Limit bright color to the primary action.

rules.tradeoff: Stark design is deliberately serious; playfulness undercuts it at every turn.
rules.resolution: Choose one. If you need both, keep stark structure and limit play to a single illustration or animation.

rules.tradeoff: Experimental layouts reward effort; approachable design asks for none.
rules.resolution: Keep navigation and controls conventional. Let the experimental side live in headlines and imagery.

rules.tradeoff: Rugged design is about durability and use; sensory design is about texture and feeling.
rules.resolution: Lead with the functional layout. Use sensory color and imagery on summary screens only.

rules.tradeoff: Emotive design asks people to feel something; functional design asks them to finish something.
rules.resolution: Keep task flows functional. Put emotive moments before and after the task, never during it.

rules.tradeoff: Bold graphic shapes demand attention; calm design lets attention rest.
rules.resolution: Use one bold graphic element per screen and keep the rest quiet.

rules.tradeoff: Stark contrast keeps people at a distance; warmth invites them in.
rules.resolution: Keep the stark type and layout, and bring warmth in through color temperature only.

rules.tradeoff: Expressive design is meant to be noticed; sober design is meant to disappear behind the task.
rules.resolution: Keep the sober base. Express character only in the display typeface.
